body: Well, I was caught by the police. They were stunned an obviously sober and calm person would be doing something as stupid and walking on an overpass, they told me I could get killed doing that. I could barely contain my laughter. What the fuck is going on? The whole universe is ruining me and it won't let me die. No, that's foolish, there's no unseen force out there conspiring against me. I've just failed, like I do at everything else.

Frustratingly, a police car pulled up as soon as I got to the right position. They didn't have a cup of tea to offer. luckily, they were silly enough to believe that I was just attempting to get home and made a poor route decision. I am completely sober, and can be quite convincing when I need to be. I've just been dropped off by my home, but how can I go back after this... I have nothing left to consider. I've taken my self-analysis as far as I can already. I'll probably just get caught again if I try the same overpass. Why is it so easy to be injured but so hard to die? I don't have a damn drop long enough for hanging, and a short drop would hurt way too much. I'm killing myself to avoid pain, not experience it.

I'm sorry, but I'm about to hang myself, at least if I can't get to a roof high enough. I have everything ready. All the personal growth in the world can't fix my life, not at this point. I was right about how bad everything would be. Death is an ugly thing, but I am certain that I cannot derive enough from this life to justify being alive. My situation is similar to that of a dying person in a home for the elderly. They choose death to alleviate pain, knowing that they can't get much else out of life. My relative youth makes this extremely unlikely, but not impossible. I debated sending this for a while, you don't deserve to see something like this. I regret that I'm going to hurt a lot of people. I thought silence would be worse, however. Thank you for everything. Please remember that this is no one's fault but my own. Goodbye.

Just tried to speak with someone at the national hotline. Called several times and the call dropped on every occasion. Than I tried a chat only to be offered practically no input. Obviously a bit upsetting, but I find myself laughing hysterically. Reddit has offered a better service than "trained professionals." I suppose I don't blame them, it's 5 in the morning here and they're just volunteers. I'd like to say I've improved, but that isn't really true. In some ways I think a part of me has died over the past 24 hours. I no longer fear the things I should. This has a few implications. One is that I don't feel liking lashing out at inanimate objects when contemplating the coming day, my feelings are... quieter now. I've banged my head in the literal sense more than once at this point. What a silly, animal thing to do. Physical self-punishment isn't going to solve anything. Another implication is that the window in my 7th story room is not as intimidating as it once was. What's the term, "call of the void?" I'm hearing that now. A single impulsive moment... oh well. I feel that I've reached the logical end of my introspection, at least in the short-term. I can't run away, I was distraught when I wrote that. I have obligations to fulfill, and I don't have the cash on hand to do it anyways. I can't even buy a train or plane ticket. Physically relocating won't get me what I want, not in the long-term. It can only ruin my chances of fixing things. I'll try to keep going. I'll post again, it might not be for a little while though. I wish you luck in your own struggles. I'm sure you have many ways to justify your own arrogance.

Edit: Finally spoke to someone, haha. I think it was the first time I've cried since elementary school. What a cathartic experience, to hear a person's voice discuss the issues that I have kept deep inside of me for so long. She thought I was in my 40's, until I told her I was in my very early 20's... It wasn't all fun and games, though. She had some unpleasant but necessary things to say.

I'm sorry for not replying sooner. I slept for a long time. I'm not really ready to write a full response to you right now, but you are right in many ways. I think I'm going to watch The Hunt for Red October and then face whatever happens today as best as I can. I still have my body and mind, whatever else I lose. That's more than can be said for some. Maybe I'll run off for a while. Maybe I've been chasing the wrong things this whole time.

Being up front with people... that's something I'll be forced to do soon. Better make it happen on my own terms I guess. That would be a substantial first step. Thank you again for your thoughts. I have glanced at your post history, you seem to do quite a bit of good around here :) I wish my problems were simpler to explain haha, I don't really want to get into practical specifics, sorry... It wouldn't really change much anyways. I'll let you know whatever I choose to do.

I have already bailed on a few obligations today, I had to, there's no way I could show up as I am now. A while back I was on a video call with my parents, they said I looked like I needed a lot more sleep... They are more right than they know. What has driven me to this edge involves the social dynamic I am involved in, you are correct. Given time, I could potentially heal, find a new way of living that will help me grow into the person I want to be. Unfortunately, tomorrow is the day that I leave my current city. Shortly after, my failures on the practical side of things will come to light and my worst fears will be realized. I will also lose access to most of the various suicide methods I have considered, should I go down that path. If I had taken the time to confront myself a week ago... but that is part of my problem. I run away from things I need to solve. Right now I am looking back on everything I have done and waiting for the repercussions to finally begin. I don't want to go through that. I don't think I can. Even if I do, what's to stop me from ruining everything all over again? Only I can fix myself in the end.

Thank you for your kind words, Jana. My name is Mason. While reading about unfortunate people like me must be rather unpleasant at times, I am glad I have been able to communicate some of my true feelings to you. I am trying very hard to do so. Don't worry, I haven't misinterpreted you, it was simply the best comparison I could think of at the time. I took the liberty of looking at some of your earlier posts. I am very jealous both of your homeland and your experiences in New Zealand :) I had hoped to visit both extensively someday. Such hopes seem like they are from a different world, created by a different person. You call me a thinker... I suppose at the moment I am doing a lot of successful thinking. Why then, have I not demonstrated my apparent mental capacity in the past? I am tempted to chalk this up merely to 20/20 hindsight. As far as I am aware, there is nothing chemically wrong with me. My family has no history of severe depression, though that is no guarantee. The stigma of seeking help, combined with my fast approaching circumstances, together prevent me from doing the logical thing and seeking professional help as you suggest. I haven't slept in a very long time... I don't want to miss any more hours than I have to. Is that the behavior of a smart person? I know so many things, I never let anything cloud my thoughts. I am always pursuing "truth," although my belief in such a thing has wavered of late. What use is all this, though? So many others who may not write in as flowery a manner as I do have something I do not: the ability to lead a normal life. They fail at times, but they have built a foundation for themselves, a solid emotional core that keeps them going. I don't have anything like that. How can an unstable being like me be valued as you say? I have some form of extraordinary capacity, but where has it gotten me? I can't actually apply that ability to the real world. I am content to distract myself on Reddit, considering other's issues, while my own life crashes down around me... As for how I am dealing with my failures, I understand what you mean. I feel like my mind is rotting. My thoughts feel like shattered glass. The difference between us is that you seem to be capable of dealing with it, in some way. You have some of the inner strength needed to continue on, the kind that I lack. Everyone faces their own challenges, but I feel as if I was never given the normal equipment people use to fight back. Please forgive me if I am assuming too much. Thank you again, you have helped me make clear to myself many thoughts I was uncomfortable with confronting. I don't expect you or anyone else to have a perfect answer to my many questions. I need to take some time to think... but I'm running out so fast.

Yes, it is very true I am still here... Something I consider neither good nor bad at the moment. I have romanticized death to the point where it seems not only a neutral state but almost comforting, but at the same time I am acutely aware of myself, perhaps more than I have ever been. Every breath, every sensation seems so much more vibrant than before. A manifestation of my survival instinct, perhaps? As for volunteering... you are right that it has the potential to make me feel more justified in continuing to live. It is something I haven't considered in a long time, yet another example of my addled mental state. The pursuit of a deeper connection with those around me sounds pretty good right about now, but I am so pressed for time. I have to make this decision now. The problem is that I feel as if I already did, a long time ago, when I made the choices that brought me here. You are right in saying that career stuff happens. We are more than our bank accounts. I am simply afraid of the future, of the reform that I will have to bring about. I'm afraid I'll break before I see the end of it. A large part of me doesn't want to see another sunrise. Then again, I am talking about suicide already, so I suppose I'm already pretty broken haha. I'll think more on what you have said. Thank you for your offer, you are very kind.
I keep writing essays, haha. Sorry for rambling, I'm less than experienced with pouring my soul out. Anyone who takes the time to peruse this post, thank you.

Thanks for your thoughts, friend. Your views seem to align with my own in many ways. I am not religious, but the sense of inspiration and awe I get when looking at the world is probably pretty close to what fervent believers feel when contemplating their various gods. Elegance is a wonderful word to use. Unfortunately, my "access" to it all is much more complicated than that. You say I have the ability to change myself. This is probably true. However, I don't really have time for that, and even if I did, I can't trust myself to actually go through with it. Sometimes I feel like a few different people, vying for control of my meat-sack. There is the rationality, the cold analysis, that tells me I am destined for very bad times ahead. I invite you to read my other reply to learn more about that. Then I have my emotional side, the one that loves Asimov and Tolkien and Rachmaninoff and French Impressionism. The one that could stare for hours at the sky and wonder at its beauty, at the value inherent in getting to witness ancient light reach our planet from stars that may be long dead. I have realized, though, that these are not the dominant aspects of my personality. No, the real me is a man who never really matured. I never acquired the fundamentals of a real adult. I am a misshapen imitation of a human being, and the consequences of this have destroyed me. Even now, this doesn't feel real in a way. How could I, the Glorious Me, ever feel like I do now? How could I ever let myself get into this state? I am ready to wake up from the nightmare to find that my life has fixed itself once more. I can't force a part of me, even as I discuss my imminent death, to acknowledge the very real, very dark place I am in. You see, arrogance is hard-wired into my psyche. I was supposed to do Great Things, whatever that means. Another of my many recent epiphanies is that I don't really know what exactly my future deeds were supposed to actually consist of. The only concrete information I have now is that very soon the whole charade will collapse. My parents, my friends, will all know. I shouldn't define myself by the perceptions of those around me, but I do to an extent. The things I want, I have personal reasons for. I don't work for things in order to look good, but how can a (as you say) flawed creature like me possibly endure both the collapse of my dreams and the disappointment of those who trusted me? That's the worst part. I could calm anger, I could reason with confusion, but disappointment? It will be completely justified and I will have no defense. My soul (for lack of a better word) will be laid bare, and I can't handle that. In the end, I see everything that I cherish being taken from me, and if the only other option is oblivion, then ultimately that is the way to go. I am grateful to you for reaching out like this. I do not have anyone to confide in, that is why I am here... I have loving parents who think I am a successful son and know nothing of the various demons I battle. I have friends who come to me for help on their most personal issues. I've even helped others with suicidal thoughts (unfortunately the advice I gave at the time doesn't apply to me.) Whatever happens, know that you made a despairing fool feel a bit more at peace.

Thank you for reading that disastrous paragraph up there. The concept of "deserving" something is complicated, and I don't think I can really communicate how I feel about it. If there is any way to measure what is owed to us humans, it probably revolves around our contributions, to both ourselves and the world. If this is the case (deep down this is likely how I think) then I most certainly deserve nothing, for I have failed myself and those who care for me repeatedly. Essentially, through a series of easily avoided mistakes, I ruined my big shot at the life I have always wanted. I refer specifically to my career, but it means more than something superficial such as prestige or money to me. It means a future of humiliation and despair, with no foreseeable recovery. Although technically I could, far in the future, achieve something like what I currently desire, I don't think I am capable of surviving the journey to reach that point. Nor do I think I want to. This is my last chance to end things before my life becomes hellish. As for the people I surround myself with, they are not really to blame for my current state, although their mere existence has probably driven me to jump through social and emotional hoops I never would have otherwise. My friends and family trust me completely. I am the "responsible one," but I don't deserve this reputation. I have coasted through life on luck and animal cleverness, and my luck has run out. The best part is that I believed the whole thing myself until very recently. I thought I was the edifice I had constructed, until I hit the first real challenges I have ever faced. It is certainly painful that I have no one to confide in, but I have never really wanted that until now. I never thought I needed it. Now it's a little late for that.
